clues.title: Road line: Black car meta
text: While driving on the right side, yellow outer lines with white middle lines are commonly found in Jordan, Israel, and the UAE. The black back of the Google car without an antenna can help confirm you’re in Jordan 100%.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Roads in Jordan typically feature yellow outside and white middle lines.
**NOTE:** Other Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE and Israel can also have these road lines. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Madaba Fields
text: Near and in the city of Madaba, you will find flat fields which are sometimes tilled. They uniquely have the characteristic of rich, red soil.
NOTE: The fields continue both north and south of Madaba, along Highway 35.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Black Car
text: Coverage in Jordan was taken by a black Google car, without a red brake light.
Jordan is the only Middle Eastern country where a black Google car without an antenna or a red brake light can be found.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: Jordanian licence plates are white and can be long or short.
Commercial transport vehicles, such as taxis, have a distinctive green strip on the left.
In the Middle East, the green strip is only found in Jordan.
The UAE also uses long white plates.
Israel however only uses yellow licence plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture
text: Most buildings in Jordan are made of bright sandstone bricks and have flat roofs.
Similar sandstone bricks are also common in Jerusalem.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons
text: Jordanian chevrons are white with red arrows.
You can use chevrons to distinguish between Jordan and Israel:
The Israeli chevrons are black with white arrows.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
